html:
The Guachichiles were a Native American people of north central Mexico. Before the Spanish came they held the largest territory of any of the Chichimec peoples, across Zacatecas, San Luis Potosí and parts of Guanajuato, Jalisco and Coahuila.

They were nomadic hunters and gatherers, known for painting their bodies and hair red. When Spanish silver mines and roads pushed into their land after 1546, they became the hardest fighters of the Chichimeca War, raiding wagon trains along the silver road with the Zacatecos.

The war ended around 1590 through gifts of food and cloth, missions, and the settling of Christian Tlaxcalan families in new towns among the Guachichiles. The city of San Luis Potosí was founded in their land in 1592. Over the next century they merged into the mixed colonial population. See also Guachichil on the modern map.
